A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bird-MAE and prototypical probing. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F in v2 and A–G in v4 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original BirdSet ablations, full-data and few-shot experiments, and AS-20k prototypical-pooling results, including supplementary results in Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds AS-20k frozen-feature probing and MeerKAT transfer results in Table 8 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The pretraining recipe, prototypical pooling equation, class-specific heads, orthogonality loss, and frozen-encoder probing procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies that probing is parametric without introducing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Table 8(b) and Appendix G add MeerKAT evaluation, extending coverage to mammal vocalizations classified by eleven call types—a distinct population and task from bird-species recognition. BirdSet and AS-20k coverage remain; AS-20k was already evaluated in v2.

E2.justification: The BirdSet comparators and probing alternatives are retained. Table 8 preserves the Audio-MAE and BEATs fine-tuning comparisons; BEATsiter2 is shortened to BEATs with the same result. Added transfer experiments reuse existing models and probing methods.

E3.justification: Table 10 changes Audio-MAE’s stated sampling rate from 32 to 16 kHz, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Table 6 newly marks supervised POW entries as validation results. Added evaluations include AS-20k frozen probing and a MeerKAT protocol using a 20% test split, half the remaining data for training, five-second segmentation, and mixup probability 0.5.

E4.justification: The original curation, pooling, model-size, training-duration, and prototype-count ablations remain. v4 adds a focused analysis of frozen-feature transfer beyond birds and newly reports that time warping did not improve validation performance in Appendix D.1.

E5.justification: Three-run averaging, three independently sampled few-shot subsets, and standard-deviation reporting were already present. Figure 4 and the uncertainty reporting in Tables 11–12 are retained without new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 6 replaces several supervised-baseline values, including Perch on PER from 18.77 to 18.23 and BirdNeXt on HSN from 45.72 to 47.29. Core Bird-MAE results remain unchanged. Table 8 adds AS-20k probing scores of 13.19 versus 17.97 and MeerKAT results, including prototypical probing scores of 28.30 for Audio-MAE and 34.58 for Bird-MAE.

T1.justification: The prototype-similarity equation, parameter-count expressions, and Appendix B metric definitions are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain domain-specific pipeline adaptation, Bird-MAE’s claimed BirdSet superiority, effective prototypical probing, and the few-shot benchmark. Clarified prototype-learning provenance and additional transfer evidence do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: The brief future-work discussion becomes a substantive Discussion and Limitations section. v4 addresses upfront pretraining costs, interprets cross-species transfer, considers model scale and SSL objective as unresolved alternative explanations, and explicitly distinguishes prior prototype interpretability evidence from analysis of Bird-MAE itself.

D1.justification: Anonymous code/model references are replaced with named GitHub and Hugging Face resources. Appendix G documents MeerKAT processing and training, while Section 6 explicitly documents masked inference for BirdNeXt and Appendix D.1 clarifies omission of time warping. Hardware and most existing hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references concerning MeerKAT/animal2vec, SpecAugment, BirdNET, population-density estimation, and active learning, and removes the Speech Commands reference. It clarifies the application of prior prototype layers while retaining the broader SSL and bioacoustic positioning.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the abstract, introduction, probing explanation, and ending. The combined Conclusion and Future Work section becomes separate Discussion and Limitations and Conclusion sections. Terminology and front matter are revised, while most methodological and experimental exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 8 expands from a small fine-tuning table into two panels with probing and fine-tuning columns. Tables 6–7 gain explicit evaluation-mode labels; tables and Figure 5 are repositioned, and journal headers are added. Existing figure graphics and most table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional transfer evidence in Table 8, explicit limitations in Section 7, and clearer implementation and access documentation modestly strengthen the paper. These additions better support and qualify broader applicability. The transfer study remains preliminary, and unexplained baseline-value and sampling-rate revisions limit the improvement in experimental transparency.
